lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: fraud and password safety

objective: Learners evaluate invented password and account-security practices and choose the ones that actually reduce risk.
scenario: Levi is an invented fifth grader reviewing a pretend list of habits for a family simulation: one password reused everywhere, a password written on a note taped to a screen, a long unique passphrase kept in a locked manager, and a habit of clicking links inside account emails. Nothing here describes a real account.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.
Never write any real password on this sheet; discuss only the invented habits listed here.

tasks.directions: Go through Levi's four invented habits one at a time. Two make an attacker's job easier and two make it harder. Say what each habit does before ranking anything.

prompts.text: Which of Levi's four habits reduce risk, and what does each of the risky ones actually make possible?

tasks.directions: Levi has to recommend a short set of practices someone would actually follow. Write the recommendation and defend it against the objection that strong passwords are too hard to remember.

prompts.text: What should Levi recommend, and how does the recommendation answer the objection that it is too hard to remember?

tasks.directions: One habit was about links rather than passwords.

prompts.text: Why is how someone reaches a login page as important as the strength of the password?

remediation: If a learner ranks habits without reasons, ask for each one what an attacker would gain, and rebuild the ranking from those answers.
extension: Ask the learner to write the one sentence Levi could say to a family member who insists on reusing one password.
